deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 'Teichmüller' notes of 1983, the same period and themes as the Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, base points, cellular 'dessins'). X_ξ is the elliptic curve with complex multiplication by i (j = 1728), so X_ξ = C/Γ_ξ with Γ_ξ = Z[i] a square lattice. Its group of automorphisms fixing the origin e is μ_4(C) ≅ Z/4Z, generated by multiplication by i.

(1) The page opens mid-sentence. It characterises η_ξ as the unique point of the 2-torsion ₂X_ξ, other than e, that is fixed by Aut(X_ξ). Concretely η_ξ = (1+i)/2 mod Γ, since i·(1+i)/2 = (i−1)/2 ≡ (1+i)/2 mod Γ. Grothendieck then strengthens this to Fix(i) = {x | ix = x} = {e, η_ξ}. This holds because 1−i has degree |1−i|² = 2, so ker(1−i) has order 2. The other two 2-torsion points, η' = 1/2 and η'' = i/2, are exchanged by i.

(2) Cell structures on the torus.
- The basic structure is the image of the lattice grid: 1 vertex e, 2 edges (the images of the two generators, the two 'mailles' of Γ_ξ), and 1 square face.
- Its pullback under [2] = 2·id_X has 4 vertices (the 2-torsion points), 8 edges and 4 square faces. Euler characteristic 4 − 8 + 4 = 0, as it should be.
- μ_4 preserves both structures, so Z/4Z ≅ μ_4(C) is a common automorphism group of the two cellular structures.

(3) Quotient by ±1. The finer structure suits X_ξ/±1 ≅ P^1, the Weierstrass ℘-map, which he denotes φ.
- The 4 vertices are the fixed points of −1, so they give 4 vertices downstairs: e^φ, η^φ, η'^φ, η''^φ, the four branch points.
- The 8 edge midpoints are 4-torsion points not fixed by −1, so the edges pair up into 4 edges.
- The 4 face centres are ((2k+1) + (2l+1)i)/4 mod Γ, also paired by −1, so they give 2 faces.
- Result: a sphere made of two squares glued along a square 'equator' through the four branch points (the 'pillowcase'). Euler characteristic 4 − 4 + 2 = 2.
- The residual action of μ_4/±1 ≅ Z/2 is visible on this picture: it fixes e^φ and η^φ and swaps η'^φ and η''^φ.

The purpose is to set up explicit combinatorial (cellular) models of the special elliptic curve with extra automorphisms. These are base points of M_{1,1} at j = 1728 and of the related M_{0,4} via the Legendre quotient, presumably to study the Teichmüller groupoid and Galois action on base points, as in the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical errors. The self-correction 'quatre' → 'huit' arêtes is right (4 − 8 + 4 = 0).
Minor imprecision: the 'two edges correspond to the two meshes of the lattice' should read the two generators (sides of a fundamental square); harmless.

ideas.what: The CM elliptic curve C/Z[i] with Aut ≅ μ_4. Fix(i) = {e, (1+i)/2}, characterising a distinguished 2-torsion point η.
ideas.modern_name: Elliptic curve with j = 1728, fixed points of the order-4 automorphism
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the special points j = 0, 1728 of M_{1,1} as base points, but not this computation

ideas.what: Square cell decomposition of the torus (1 vertex, 2 edges, 1 face) and its pullback by multiplication by 2 (4, 8, 4), with μ_4 as common automorphism group.
ideas.modern_name: Regular map {4,4} on the torus; dessin d'enfant / clean map on a CM elliptic curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Coxeter–Moser (regular maps); Grothendieck/Belyi framework for dessins
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), general discussion of cellular maps / dessins and regular maps on elliptic curves

ideas.what: Quotient X/±1 ≅ P^1 as a 'pillowcase': two squares glued along an equator through the four images of the 2-torsion points.
ideas.modern_name: Pillowcase orbifold (2,2,2,2); Weierstrass ℘-map as a cellular map
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; pillowcase terminology from later work on square-tiled surfaces (Eskin–Okounkov, Thurston et al.)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard computation of cell structures on the square-lattice elliptic curve and its pillowcase quotient. It shows how Grothendieck concretely built base-point 'dessins' for the Teichmüller tower, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: First line likely reads 'comme l'unique point ≠ e de ₂(X_ξ) qui est fixé par Aut(X_ξ) ≃ Z/4Z' — ₂(X_ξ) denotes the 2-torsion subgroup.
'(X_ξ)^{i id}' is the fixed-point set of i·id, i.e. X^{i}.
'ces arêtes correspondant aux deux mailles' is an insertion above the line; 'huit' replaces struck 'quatre'; '4' is inserted before 'faces'.
The struck word before X_ξ/±1 is illegible (transcribed 'Eb(8)'); its reading is uncertain.
The superscript on the vertices is likely φ, the quotient map X → X/±1: e^φ, η^φ, η'^φ, η''^φ.
